target.title: chore: enable array fill lint rule
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Oxlint 1.72 added `unicorn/no-array-fill-with-reference-type`, which catches arrays whose elements accidentally share one mutable object. OpenClaw currently inherits the rule through the broad `suspicious` category, but the curated rule list does not record that policy explicitly.

Follow-up to #100027 and #100083.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Pins `unicorn/no-array-fill-with-reference-type` at error severity.
- Preserves the existing effective lint behavior while making the intended guard durable and reviewable.
- Avoids enabling the noisy style-only rules introduced in the same Oxlint release.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior change. Future attempts to initialize an array with one shared mutable reference fail lint explicitly.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox-through-Crabbox: `tbx_01kwqt12gtgnft4w8wxepgt8dx`.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed.
- Full `pnpm lint`: core 0 warnings/errors; plugins 0 warnings/errors; scripts 0 warnings/errors.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Fresh Codex autoreview: clean, 0.99 confidence.

AI-assisted implementation and review.
